description.main: Catalogue of the 2014-15 Fundación MAPFRE retrospective of Alvin Langdon Coburn, with a technical atlas of his work by Anne Cartier-Bresson.
description.extended:
Catalogue of the Fundación MAPFRE retrospective of Alvin Langdon Coburn (1882-1966), the Pictorialist who went on to make some of the first abstract photographs.

The volume, curated by Pamela Glasson Roberts, runs from Coburn's early work of 1900-1905 through portraits, views of Britain and Europe, and the New York, Niagara Falls, Pittsburgh, Yosemite and Grand Canyon series of 1909-1912. Later sections cover the Vortographs and multiple exposures of 1914-1917, the Liverpool Cathedral pictures, his late work and his paintings. Anne Cartier-Bresson contributes a technical atlas of his processes, and a chronology closes the book. The exhibition was shown at Fundación Mapfre in Madrid and then at George Eastman House in Rochester.

Coburn was born in Boston. In 1912 he photographed New York from skyscraper heights, working with the artist-poet Max Weber. He published the portrait book Men of Mark in 1913 and moved to London in 1914, joining the Vorticists. After 1920 he withdrew to rural Wales to paint, compose music and pursue Freemasonry. Beaumont and Nancy Newhall championed him again in the 1950s, and he left almost 20,000 prints and negatives to George Eastman House.
